motionExceptions.reason: brief: "His closed happy eyes keep their exact drawn shape and proportions throughout... they never squash, stretch, or squint... their own scale has to cancel the body's out" — the eyes' scale track is the exact inverse of the body's squash/stretch (product 100%), never a blink or a squint.
brief: "The pale ribbon stays still" — it holds its source position for the whole loop while the body bounces near it; not welded to the mascot.

brief: "The bright swoosh and its spark answer his landings too: on each impact they dip a couple of pixels and recover, a frame or two behind him, at low amplitude derived from his own bounce" — a small world-response DERIVED from the mascot's own LANDINGS clock (same technique as the shadow), not a parented/welded part of the body.
same as above — the spark shares the swoosh's exact landing-dip clock and amplitude.
the gleam strokes ride the ribbon's own static path; see the ribbon exception.

brief: "The pale ribbon stays still" while the swoosh now dips a couple of px on every landing — their touching edge (the ribbon's head meeting the swoosh's start) genuinely opens and closes by the dip amplitude on each impact, a brief-directed divergence between a static element and a landing-responsive one.
stage-fixed ribbon passing near the face, not welded to it.
the swoosh's small landing-dip passes near the air-flow marks; both are independently driven off the mascot's own LANDINGS clock (derived, not welded).
the swoosh's small landing-dip passes near the face, not welded to it.

swoosh and spark share the IDENTICAL landing-dip function (same lag, same amplitude) so they move in lockstep with each other; the residual is the spark's own pop scaling around its own artwork centre (scale-pivot gate) at the entrance, not an independent clock.
